scope: HOST read-only source and preserved API35 observations; no ADB, source edits, new tests or device-scope expansion
confirmed_causal_path: Logcat uses MutableSharedFlow<String>() with zero replay/extra capacity; its IO producer calls suspend emit once per included record.
LogView launches collection in lifecycleScope (Main context); collectLines inherits that context for onLine -> LogAdapter.append.
Each included line therefore requires producer/subscriber rendezvous and Main work. postOnAnimation batches RecyclerView notifications, not the IO-to-Main per-line delivery.
When Main delivery/processing is slower than logcat stdout production, the producer stops draining stdout while waiting; a finite stdout pipe can exert backpressure on the logcat child.
The two LogBuffers bound text retained after arrival at the adapter (each 10000 records / 2097152 UTF16 units); they do not promise that collection has caught up to the live logd suffix.
The same zero-buffer SharedFlow and Main subscriber design exists at base12; this observation is not evidence of a new e8-specific throughput regression.

capture_driver.observation: Periodic capture only; no jump-to-bottom or scroll injection in its loop.

first_memory_segment.scope: Completed first 600-second sampler segment only; native terminal/export/lifecycle still pending. Discrete samples, not an instantaneous peak or formal performance result.

important_limits: flow06 visible old timestamps cannot by themselves measure reader/retained-tail delay: append does not auto-scroll, and capture driver does not jump to bottom. A preserved scroll anchor can show earlier rows even if newer records exist.
pipe_write is a point-in-time stdout backpressure observation, not proof of deadlock or a permanently blocked reader.
No missing source line, logd overwrite, lost line count, throughput ceiling, or latency P95 is established by this review.
No hard leak or exact all-heap memory cap follows from bounded adapter text; the stated 2-window cap concerns retained record text only.
The memory segment is finite/discrete and includes native dictionary maintenance; it is not a long-run performance result or proof that allocations are flat under all loads.
pr_wording_recommendation: Bounds the displayed/exported suffix of records received by the view, with explicit omission notice and owned reader cleanup. It does not guarantee real-time freshness during sustained high-volume output; catch-up rate, source logd loss and source-to-screen latency remain unqualified.

bug_assessment.definite_architecture_limitation: There is no decoupled IO ingestion or throughput/freshness guarantee; Main per-line rendezvous can backpressure the child under sustained output.
bug_assessment.possible_future_minimal_design: If live-tail freshness becomes a required contract, batch/queue received records on IO using a bounded suffix buffer, then drain a bounded batch to Main per frame with source order and explicit omission accounting. Keep process ownership/cancellation tests. Adding finite extra SharedFlow capacity alone only postpones sustained overload, and DROP_OLDEST without omission accounting would silently change diagnostic semantics.
bug_assessment.current_action: Do not change production code or enlarge the current device scope. Complete the already frozen original-APK lifecycle/export/17-item and T9 scopes; report this limitation separately.
